F-02.finding: The application channel is contradictory. The calendar sends Saudi applicants to Qabool and non-Saudis to Study in Saudi, while other pages send everyone to the PMU portal.
F-02.where: P14 /admission/admission_calendar_fs_ro · P02 · P04 · P17 · P18 · P19 · P15 portal
F-02.current: P14: "For Saudi Students: Apply online through Qabool platform: https://www.uap.sa/" · "For non Saudi Students: Apply online through Study in Saudi platform … Closed". The same page carries two "Apply Now" buttons to https://pmu.edu.sa/Apply.
F-02.conflicting: P18: "The application process can be completed entirely online" → pmu.edu.sa/apply. P17 and P19 → http://admissions.pmu.edu.sa/ (“Complete online application”). P03, P04, P06, P07, P09, P14, P17, P19, P28 → ../Admission/Apply_Now_ADS.aspx (→ /admission/apply_now_ads). The hub → https://www.pmu.edu.sa/apply; P02 and P18 → https://pmu.edu.sa/apply. The Medicine academic page (P54) “Apply Now” → the Medicine admission information page, not an application channel. P09 → uap.sa. Live DOM probe 2026-09-27: at least 4 different endpoints behind the same “Apply” label (../evidence/dom-probes-2026-09-27.md).
F-02.screenshot: S14: "Apply Now" button next to the Qabool instruction on the same page. S15: portal "Register" with no routing guidance.
F-02.impact: Applicants may apply on the wrong platform and miss the decision cycle. International applicants are told an online route exists that the calendar marks Closed.
F-02.treatment: Define one channel per applicant type. Make every Apply CTA a routing step (Saudi / non-Saudi / transfer / graduate).

F-03.finding: The Medicine application fee differs by SAR 150 between two official pages.
F-03.current: P09: "Pay a non-refundable application fee of SAR 1000 (incl. VAT)".
F-03.conflicting: P12: "Medical Application Fee — SAR 1,150 (VAT inclusive)". P13 (Other Fees) omits a Medicine fee.
F-03.screenshot: S12 shows "SAR 1,150 (VAT inclusive)" directly. The SAR 1000 value is quoted from P09 text (below the screenshot fold).
F-03.impact: Money charged differs from money advertised, a consumer-protection risk.
F-03.treatment: Finance confirms the value. Render it from one fee record on both pages.

F-04.finding: English-proficiency thresholds conflict, and one uses a test format retired about 20 years ago.
F-04.current: P03: exempt with "TOEFL score of 513 (CBT 183, iBT 65) … or IELTS Band of 5.5 … (5.5 writing)".
F-04.conflicting: P04/P06: IELTS 6.0 overall / 5.5 writing for Core/direct entry. P07: TOEFL iBT 83 / writing 19 for Core. P20: "TOEFL or IELTS of 550" (no IELTS 550 exists). CBT retired 2006 (X02). TOEFL moved to a 1–6 scale on 21 Jan 2026 (X01).
F-04.screenshot: S03 (Freshman page identity). Threshold text quoted from P03, P06 and P07.
F-04.impact: The same applicant is exempt on one page and placed in Prep on another. Prep adds cost (SAR 30,000 per semester, P11).
F-04.treatment: Publish one threshold table with a 1–6 TOEFL mapping and an effective date. Delete CBT/PBT references.

F-05.finding: Tahseely equivalence for SAT applicants is stated three ways, one of them impossible.
F-05.conflicting: P19: "(SAAT – Tahseely) or SAT 1 (1200)". P18: "SAT II 30%" (Subject Tests discontinued 2021, X06). P28 SAT page: "SAT with minimum score of 1200 instead of Qudrat and Tahseely tests". P03 does not mention Tahseely.
F-05.impact: International and SAT applicants cannot satisfy or interpret the rule.
F-05.treatment: Decide the valid Tahseely equivalent and publish it once.

F-08.finding: The calendar is stale for the audit date and does not match the portal.
F-08.current: On 2026-09-27, P14 shows only "Fall 2026-2027" (classes began 2026-08-30). There is no next-intake status. Results (Jul 19–21) overlap the IELTS/TOEFL and transfer deadline (Jul 20).
F-08.conflicting: P15 portal: "No events are currently published." Portal banner advertises graduate admission for "الفصل الدراسي الثاني 2026/2025" (past, year order reversed). Footer "Academic Calendar" → academic_calendar_2021_2022_ro.aspx.
F-08.screenshot: S14 (calendar), S15 (portal "No events" and the banner).
F-08.impact: Applicants cannot tell whether admissions are open. They get conflicting signals from the site and the portal.
F-08.treatment: Add an "intake status" component driven by the canonical calendar and shown on the site and the portal. Fix the footer link.

F-09.current: P19: "the minimum weighted total, defined by the Admissions Office, should be met". P18: "Acceptable SAT I". P04/P17: "equivalent TOEFL iBT with acceptable scores".
F-09.conflicting: P07 gives TOEFL numbers but P04/P17 do not link to them in context.
F-09.impact: The admission decision rests on an unpublished number. This is a transparency and appeal risk.
F-09.treatment: Publish the minimum composite per program, or state explicitly that it varies by cycle, with a date.

F-10.finding: Fee information is fragmented across generations and entry points.
F-10.current: P10 lists "Fall Semester 2026/2027", "Fall Semester 2025/2026" and "Continuing Students 2024–2025" side by side with no "current" label. The hub links Fees_TF_RO.aspx while the Freshman page links Tuition_Fees_RO.aspx.
F-10.conflicting: P13 has no effective date and omits the Medicine fee. Fees live under the Registration Office breadcrumb, outside the admissions journey.
F-10.impact: Applicants may read an outdated schedule.
F-10.treatment: One fee page per intake, labelled current and past. Archive expired schedules with a clear banner.

F-11.finding: Contact routing is broken or misdirected.
F-11.where: P01 · P02–P20 sidebars · P15 · all footers
F-11.current: Undergraduate sidebars "Contact Info" → Admission_Contact_GDP.aspx (the graduate contact page). Hub "Contact Us" → staff directory. Portal "Contact Admissions" → the hub, which has no contact details. Footer "Directory" and "SiteMap" → "#".
F-11.conflicting: P21 and the Web Admission Guide (P55) publish named individual staff phone numbers and emails instead of role mailboxes. The hub "Contact Us" opens a Student Affairs staff list with no admissions role (P63). Contact Us lists "financal_aid@pmu.edu.sa" (misspelt), while the MOHE PDF uses "financial_aid@pmu.edu.sa" (P64/P66). No mailbox is labelled Admissions.
F-11.impact: Undergraduate applicants reach graduate staff or dead ends.
F-11.treatment: One admissions contact component (role mailboxes, phone, hours, query form).

F-13.finding: Required documents differ by page for the same route.
F-13.current: P03: "Original Secondary School Certificate", "Saudi ID or Iqama". P04: "Copy of secondary school certificate", "Copy of Saudi ID" (no Iqama path). P18: "Copy of National ID", certificate "certified by the Saudi Cultural Mission and Saudi Embassy".
F-13.conflicting: P02: international-school transcripts must be MoE-attested, plus an equivalency letter.
F-13.treatment: One document checklist per applicant type, generated from the canonical record.

F-15.current: The hub is a list of about 40 links with no introduction, status or routing. Two templates coexist. Freshman (P03) and Direct Admissions (P04) describe the same route with different rules. The "Core" level is never defined. P19 is titled "CS & Engineering" but also covers Architecture. P08 prints six raw URLs.
F-15.conflicting: Breadcrumbs vary (P04 ends "> Freshman"; P03 and P20 lack "Home").
F-15.impact: Excess navigation, and applicants pick the wrong route.

F-17.finding: Typos and grammar errors on policy pages.
F-17.where: P01 "Visting Students" · P19 "wave" · P09 "were 86", "College of Medical" · P17 "to be consider" · hub URL "MIlBL"
F-17.treatment: Editorial QA step in the publishing workflow.

F-20.finding: The Medicine composite minimum cannot be reached at the published component minimums.
F-20.current: "*20% high school + 40% Qudrat + 40% Tahseely were 86 is the minimum acceptable score". The document list states the minimums "(95%)", "(80)", "(80)".
F-20.conflicting: Recomputed: 0.2×95 + 0.4×80 + 0.4×80 = 83.0 < 86. A candidate who meets every published minimum still fails the stated composite. To reach 86 with HS 95, Qudrat and Tahseely must average at least 83.75.
F-20.impact: Applicants read the component minimums as sufficient when they are not. This misleads eligibility self-assessment.
F-20.treatment: Publish consistent minimums, or publish the composite as the only binding rule with a worked example.
F-20.owner: Dean, College of Medicine + Admissions Committee

F-21.finding: The EMGMS requirements page contains another university's checklist.
F-21.current: "Graduate English Language Endorsement from UA Center for English as Second Language (CESL)" · "TOEFL – minimum of 79 iBT (or 60 on the revised PBT…)" · "IELTS – minimum composite score of 7, with no subject area below a 6" · "Pearson PTE Academic – minimum of 60".
F-21.conflicting: X09: CESL is at the University of Arizona, and its endorsement "is for UA admission only". Every other PMU graduate page (P34–P42): "IELTS 6.0 overall and 5.5 in each skill … TOEFL iBT 83 overall and 19 in each skill".
F-21.impact: Wrong thresholds (IELTS 7 vs 6), a pathway PMU applicants cannot use, and reputational exposure.
F-21.treatment: Withdraw the page, rewrite it from PMU's graduate rule, and confirm program-specific thresholds.
F-21.owner: Dean, College of Engineering + Graduate Admissions

F-23.finding: The Medicine programme duration is stated as 7 years in one place and 6 in another.
F-23.current: P09: "The PMU College of Medical curriculum is based on a 7-year hybrid model between the US and KSA medical school structures."
F-23.conflicting: P54: "Developed in strategic collaboration with the University of Illinois Chicago (UIC), the college features a globally-aligned, 6-year integrated curriculum". P12 prices a separate "Medical Preparatory Program" (SAR 75,000/yr) and "Medical Program" (SAR 90,000/yr).
F-23.impact: Duration drives total cost (about SAR 90,000 per year) and the family's decision.
F-23.treatment: College confirms "Prep year + 6-year MD/MBBS" (or otherwise) and publishes the total programme cost.

F-25.finding: The programme catalogue differs across four surfaces.
F-25.where: P61 Degrees & Programs · P60 List of Majors · P45 Graduate Fees · P01/P33 hubs
F-25.current: P61 lists no College of Medicine, no EMGMS, no Engineering Innovation/Sustainability/Entrepreneurship programme, and no Pre-Master M.Ed.
F-25.conflicting: P45 prices "Master of Engineering in Innovation, Sustainability, and Entrepreneurship" and "PRE-Master for Master of Education". P60 names it "Master of Science in Engineering Innovation…" and also omits Medicine. The page footer "Colleges / Programs" omits Medicine. MSHD / MSEHD / "Master of Science in Education and Human Development" naming drift.
F-25.impact: Applicants cannot confirm which programmes are open for admission.
F-25.treatment: One canonical programme register (status, names AR/EN, college, admission page, fee row).
F-25.owner: Vice President for Academic Affairs (programme owner) + Admissions

F-26.finding: Admission pages have empty required sections.
F-26.where: P36 EMBA · P35 PhD-BA · P39 MSME · P44 MA IBL · P25 Prep
F-26.current: EMBA "Educational Background:" and "Personal Interview:" are empty. PhD-BA "Personal Interview:" is empty. MSME "Educational Background:" has only a footnote. MA IBL "Educational Background:" and "English Language Proficiency Test:" are empty, while it weights "30% for the written test" without describing the test. Prep "Admission Criteria" list and "Admission Process" are empty.
F-26.impact: Eligibility cannot be determined for 5 programmes.
F-26.treatment: Fill these sections from the canonical record. Add a publishing check that blocks empty required fields.

F-27.finding: The same GPA descriptor is attached to different thresholds.
F-27.where: P37 MBA · P40 MSEE · P41 MSCE · P42 MSID vs P34 PhD-ME
F-27.current: "A minimum GPA of 2.50 out of 4.00 or equivalent (Very Good)"
F-27.conflicting: P34: "A minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00 out of 4.00 or equivalent (Very Good)"
F-27.impact: Ambiguous equivalence for applicants holding 5-point or percentage transcripts.
F-27.treatment: The Registrar confirms the grading-scale descriptors. Publish a conversion table.

F-28.finding: Prep→UG page: mismatched footnotes and an undefined exit exam.
F-28.current: "* Department of Information Technology is excluded from PRPM 0022" (asterisk attached to Engineering and to Architecture & Design) · " Department of Architecture is excluded from PRPM 0012" (attached to CCES) · "Successfully pass the EXIT exam".
F-28.conflicting: The EXIT exam is not described anywhere reviewed.
F-28.impact: Students misread which maths courses apply.
F-28.treatment: Correct the footnotes. Define the exit exam and its passing standard.

F-31.finding: International transfer and visiting students are quoted two different application fees.
F-31.where: C07 /admission/international_students (Transfer Students, Visitor Students) vs C27 /admission/admission-from-other-universities · C28 /admission/visiting-student-admission
F-31.current: C07 (transfer and visitor): "Pay a non-refundable application fee of SAR 500 (excl. VAT) upon submission of documents".
F-31.conflicting: C27 and C28: "Pay a non-refundable application fee of SAR 950 (incl. VAT) upon submission of documents".
F-31.screenshot: ../remediation/linkaudit/content/shots/C07-1.jpg, ../remediation/linkaudit/content/shots/C27-1.jpg, ../remediation/linkaudit/content/shots/C28-1.jpg: each fee line highlighted in place.
F-31.impact: The same applicant is told two amounts (SAR 500 + VAT vs SAR 950 incl. VAT) and cannot tell which will be charged.
F-31.treatment: Finance confirms one fee per applicant category. Publish it from the canonical fee record on every route page.

F-32.finding: The MA in International Business Law cannot be completed in the stated time at the stated load.
F-32.current: C20: "Typically, candidates will complete the program within two years in a full-time mode (maximum 6 credits in each semester)".
F-32.conflicting: C21: "Master of Arts in International Business Law (36)". 36 credits at a maximum of 6 per semester = 6 semesters (3 academic years), not two.
F-32.impact: Applicants plan time, employment and cost on a duration the programme cannot deliver.
F-32.treatment: College of Law confirms the credit total, per-semester maximum and normal duration. Publish consistent figures.
F-32.owner: Dean, College of Law + Graduate Studies

F-33.finding: The English-test equivalence and the list of recognised tests are not defined consistently.
F-33.where: C20 (MA IBL) vs the other graduate pages · C32 /admission/overview-undergraduate-placement-tests vs C19 (EMGMS)
F-33.current: C20: "minimum scores of 6.5 overall and 5.5 in each skill or equivalent TOEFL iBT minimum scores of 83 overall".
F-33.conflicting: Nine other graduate pages treat TOEFL iBT 83 as equivalent to IELTS 6.0. C32 refers to "PMU recognized proficiency English language test certificates" and names only IELTS and TOEFL, while C19 also accepts Pearson PTE (see F-21).
F-33.impact: The same TOEFL score is equivalent to two different IELTS bands. Applicants cannot tell which tests are accepted.
F-33.treatment: Publish one concordance table (IELTS / TOEFL iBT 1–6 and 0–120 / others) and a closed list of recognised tests, with an effective date.

F-34.finding: The majors that carry specific (higher) admission requirements are listed differently.
F-34.current: C30: "These majors are Architecture, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering and Civil Engineering."
F-34.conflicting: C36 adds "Artificial Intelligence" and ends the list with "etc.". C02 lists "B.S. in Chemical Engineering" and "B.S. in Cybersecurity", which neither list mentions.
F-34.impact: Applicants to AI, Chemical Engineering or Cybersecurity cannot tell whether Tahseely and the higher thresholds apply.
F-34.treatment: Publish one closed list of majors with specific requirements, generated from the programme register.

F-35.finding: Visiting-student eligibility and documents are defined inconsistently.
F-35.current: C23 and C28: "Visiting students are students registered in other local or international recognized universities".
F-35.conflicting: C07: "registered in other international recognized universities". C28 also asks a university student for "Copy of secondary school certificate or equivalent" and "Copy of General Aptitude Test score report (Qudrat) or equivalent (SAT 1) - if available".
F-35.impact: Local visiting students may assume they are excluded. Applicants gather documents that may not be needed.
F-35.treatment: Define visiting-student eligibility once. Confirm the minimum document set.

F-36.finding: The PhD in Business Administration eligibility rule says the opposite of what it intends.
F-36.current: "Otherwise, if the master degree is not from another discipline they must successfully attend and complete with minimum GPA 2.80 12 credit hours of MBA"
F-36.conflicting: The context (a bridging requirement for non-business master's holders) requires *is from another discipline*. The two GPA conditions (3.00 cumulative vs 3.20 in "an applicable master's degree program") are not assigned to cases.
F-36.impact: An eligibility rule for a SAR 150,000 programme can be read two ways.
F-36.treatment: Rewrite the rule as a table: applicant background → bridging courses → minimum GPA.

F-37.finding: Accreditation and quality claims are imprecise or unsourced.
F-37.current: C11: "The Ph.D. program is internationally accredited by AACSB as top 6% of business schools worldwide."
F-37.conflicting: AACSB accredits business schools (institution level), and fewer than 6% of business schools hold it (AACSB’s own wording); it is not a programme ranking (X10, aacsb.edu). C01: "Texas International Education Consortium (TIEC), which is a consortium of 32 universities in Texas, USA" and "reviewed and verified by around 70 multinational academic and industrial experts". No date or source is given, and the accrediting "prestigious national and international organizations" are not named.
F-37.impact: Overstated or unverifiable claims expose the University to credibility and consumer-protection risk.
F-37.treatment: State accreditations precisely (body, scope, date) with a link to the accreditor's register. Remove unsourced figures.
F-37.owner: Quality Assurance + College of Business Administration + Communications

F-38.finding: Graduate programme coverage is incomplete on the entry pages.
F-38.current: C07 lists only "MBA", "MSHD" and "MSME" for international graduate applicants.
F-38.conflicting: The hub links 11 graduate programmes. On C09, MSCE, MSEE and MSID show "Application Form" without a link, while the other programmes have one.
F-38.impact: International applicants may conclude that only three programmes are open to them. Some applicants have no form link.
F-38.treatment: Generate both lists from the programme register, including status and eligibility for international applicants.

F-39.finding: The Medicine curriculum for Years 1–2 is written as a list of US pre-medical prerequisites, not as a PMU curriculum.
F-39.current: "Biology: One full year (2 courses) of general biology with laboratory." (similar lines for chemistry, organic chemistry, physics and behavioural science)
F-39.conflicting: The phrasing (*One full year (2 courses) of …*) describes prerequisites for entering a medical school. It does not describe courses taken at PMU (see also F-07 and F-23).
F-39.impact: Applicants cannot tell what they will study in Years 1–2 or whether prior coursework is expected.
F-39.treatment: College of Medicine rewrites the curriculum section from its approved study plan.

F-40.finding: Programme and route pages omit core facts: credit hours, duration, cost and deadlines.
F-40.current: C10 and C14 give no credit total, duration, fee or deadline. C25 states no duration or cost of the Preparatory Program.
F-40.conflicting: C21 prices the PhD-ME at "(72)" credits and SAR 150,000; the MSHD fee implies 42 credits (SAR 50,000 ÷ 1,191), but no page states it.
F-40.impact: Applicants must combine several pages to learn basic facts.
F-40.treatment: Add a standard "programme facts" block (credits, duration, mode, cost, next intake) to every programme page.

F-41.finding: Launch-era and time-bound wording leaves the programme status unclear.
F-41.current: C16 and C17: "The program will be offered under the College of Engineering." C18: "The Department of Interior Design at PMU will educate tomorrow’s interior design leaders". C20: "The year 2025 marks another milestone".
F-41.conflicting: C21 prices all four programmes as current.
F-41.impact: Applicants cannot tell whether these programmes are open for admission.
F-41.treatment: Show the admission status per programme. Rewrite the text in the present tense.

F-42.finding: Graduate requirement wording is inconsistent within and across pages.
F-42.current: C12: "Successful candidates should have from three to five years of professional work experience" and, on the same page, "Participants are required to have several years of work experience".
F-42.conflicting: C13 lists no supporting documents (no references, statement or CV), unlike every other graduate page. It is unconfirmed whether none are required.
F-42.impact: Candidates with more than five years' experience may think they are excluded. MBA applicants may submit incomplete files.
F-42.treatment: State *at least three years*. Confirm the MBA document list.

F-43.finding: Placeholder and empty sections remain on applicant pages.
F-43.current: C07: the "Transportation" section has a heading and no content. Its Housing text is in the future tense ("will be located"). C03: "Orientation for new applicants	TBA", although classes began on 2026-08-30.
F-43.impact: Applicants see unfinished information on relocation and orientation.
F-43.treatment: Complete these sections or remove them. Add a pre-publication check for empty sections.

F-44.finding: Information is hidden from applicants or left in page code.
F-44.current: C02 shows only "Undergraduate Programs" and "Graduate Programs" until the collapsed lists are opened, and the page code keeps a hidden Master of LAW entry. C07 holds international payment instructions, including bank details, only inside page code that is not displayed (not reproduced in this audit).
F-44.impact: Applicants do not see the programme list or the payment method. Hidden legacy entries can resurface.
F-44.treatment: Show the programme list openly. Decide whether to publish official payment instructions, and remove leftover code.

F-45.finding: The admission query form sets no response-time expectation and offers no alternative channel.
F-45.current: The form collects name, email, mobile and query. It does not state when a reply can be expected or give a direct phone or email alternative.
F-45.impact: Applicants cannot tell when to follow up, especially near deadlines.
F-45.treatment: State the service standard (e.g. reply within N working days) and link the admissions contact component (F-11).
